## Magu offering wine  
China, Qing dynasty (1644- 1911), 18th or early 19th century Kei (silk tapestry) hanging scroll, 135.2 x 75.7 cm Gift of Dr Lam Kwok Pun HKUT2008.1670  
Accompanied by a phoenix and a child attendant holding a ray (a wish- granting wand or scepter), the figure on this scroll is Magu, the Goddess of Longevity. According to Dawei myth, Magu became an immortal and witnessed the Eastern ocean dry up and turn into mulberry fields three times, indicating her transcendence of the Here, she carries on with the cup and a light mushroom on a platter, from which she brews longevity wine for the birthday banquet of the Queen Mother of the West. The wine peals of her headdress were painted with brushstrokes using a technique known as kkean ('silk tapestry' and painting'), which is characteristic of Kei produced during the reign of the Qing- Emperor (1736- 99). The choice of this figure - together with auspicious chrysanthemums and five bats surrounding a show (longevity) character on her dress - suggests that the tapestry was intended as a birthday present, most likely for a woman.
